questions.explain: The chapter argues accuracy comes from constraining the problem: a curated metadata contract built from sys.tables, sys.columns, sys.foreign_keys, and extended properties — not from a better model or prompt.
options: A larger LLM with more parameters
A curated, versioned metadata contract generated from SQL Server catalog views
Few-shot examples of past user questions
A higher temperature setting for more creative SQL
questions.q: According to the chapter, what is the single highest-leverage input to an accurate NLQ system?

questions.explain: The semantic layer of views eliminates ambiguous naming, business-logic guessing, and join-path explosion — the failure modes that sink naive text-to-SQL.
options: Views execute faster than tables in every case
Base tables cannot be read by a db_datareader login
Views pre-resolve ambiguous joins and bake in business definitions, removing the main sources of wrong generated SQL
The LLM cannot parse base table names
questions.q: Why should the NLQ system query curated reporting views instead of base tables?

questions.explain: Layer 2 is statement validation before execution — single SELECT/WITH only, allowlisted reporting views, forbidden DDL/DML keywords, and a TOP row cap injected when missing.
options: Running generated SQL as a sysadmin so all objects are reachable
Pre-execution statement validation: single SELECT, allowlisted views, forbidden keywords, injected TOP cap
Allowing the model to choose any schema to maximize answer coverage
Caching results for 30 days to reduce database load
questions.q: Which of the following is part of the chapter's four-layer NLQ safety architecture?

questions.explain: Scoring uses execution match (EXCEPT both directions, NULL-safe and order-independent) because many different queries can be correct; string matching would reject valid alternatives.
options: By exact string match against the expected SQL
By execution match — comparing result sets with EXCEPT in both directions
By asking the LLM whether its own SQL looks right
By measuring query execution time against a threshold
questions.q: In the golden question set evaluation harness, how is a generated query judged correct?

questions.explain: Deterministic generation means repeated questions produce identical queries — essential for trust, caching, and a meaningful golden-set regression suite.
options: To reduce API token costs
To make SQL generation deterministic so the same question always yields the same query, keeping user trust and golden-set evaluation meaningful
To prevent the model from using T-SQL-specific syntax
To speed up response latency
questions.q: Why does the NLQ pipeline set the LLM temperature to 0.0?
